reports.summary:
Two confirmed P2 findings:

- **Session response failure permanently blocks shutdown** — [redboxSession.ts:90](/mnt/docker-storage/t3/worktrees/redbox-portal/t3-815a2a6e/packages/redbox-core/src/middleware/redboxSession.ts:90). `retainHttpResponse()` sets ownership before invoking express-session’s end wrapper, but a synchronous throw before session dispatch never releases it. Reproduced with both a throwing `store.set()` and cyclic session data: the error propagates, the transport closes, and `beforeShutdown` remains pending indefinitely. Handle synchronous handoff failures separately while retaining genuinely pending session callbacks.

- **Failed GridFS copy leaves an internal stream blocking disposal** — [GridFSDriver.ts:240](/mnt/docker-storage/t3/worktrees/redbox-portal/t3-815a2a6e/packages/redbox-core/src/storage/GridFSDriver.ts:240). `copyFile()` opens a source stream tracked through `finished()` before `writeStream()` deletes the destination. If destination deletion rejects, the source is never consumed or destroyed. Consequently, `drain()` waits forever; `move()` shares this path. A fake-bucket reproduction preserved the deletion error and showed disposal completing only after manually destroying the internal stream. Destroy the source when destination preparation fails.

Both violate the lifecycle contract in [design.md §7](/mnt/docker-storage/t3/worktrees/redbox-portal/t3-815a2a6e/support/specs/waterline-retirement/design.md:495).

Standards axis: no qualifying documented-rule breaches or heuristic smell findings. No edits, containers, or builds performed; both findings were reproduced with local in-memory probes.

Spec axis: **0 qualifying findings** at `1dab20b08`.

Reviewed R5 restrictions against bundled named queries, editor output, report/dashboard criteria, related-filter projections and delivered repository semantics. I found no concrete over-refusal affecting shipped callers, new parity defect, or scope creep into the G-TX-gated work.

Existing intentional refusals have migration guidance. This read-only review adds no runtime qualification; no edits, containers, builds or tests were performed.

- **[P2] Failed session end can reacquire permanent response ownership** — [requestLifetime.ts:93](/mnt/docker-storage/t3/worktrees/redbox-portal/t3-815a2a6e/packages/redbox-core/src/middleware/requestLifetime.ts:93). `failHttpResponse` clears the flags but leaves `responseEnded` false. express-session sets its internal `ended` flag before serialization/store dispatch. After either throws, a normal error handler calling `res.status(500).end(...)` or `res.serverError(...)` sets `responsePending` again, while express-session immediately returns `false` without reaching the underlying end. A subsequent client disconnect therefore leaves shutdown draining forever. The new regressions bypass this path by calling `res.destroy()` directly. Preserve a terminal failed-end state so retries cannot reacquire response ownership, while retaining the independently tracked store callbacks.
Zero qualifying findings in the current final patch.
